title: Single-Pulse Optical Switching combined with Current-Induced Motion of Skyrmionic Spin Textures
authors: Edoardo Mangini, Duc Minh Tran, Boonthum Kunyangyuen, Jun Xiao Lin, Raphael Gruber, Michel Hehn, Stéphane Mangin, Mathias Kläui
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are promising nanoscale information carriers because their position can be manipulated by electrical currents. The additional ability of deterministic control of the spin structure would allow the use of magnetic skyrmions as multi-state bits, expanding the capabilities of skyrmion devices further. Such control could be realized by coupling all-optical helicity independent switching of magnetization (AO-HIS) to magnetic skyrmions. This is realized in a Pt/Ir/CoB/Gd/Pt multilayer that is engineered to stabilize magnetic skyrmions and, at the same time, enable AO-HIS by single ultrafast laser pulse. Laser excitation is used to write skyrmionic textures, whose polarity is selected by a small applied out-of-plane field. A single 30 fs laser pulse is then used to toggle the magnetization of an illuminated region containing skyrmionic textures, reversing their polarities without requiring any magnetic field or current pulses. This establishes deterministic optical switching of the skyrmion spin structure as a new manipulation channel, distinct from previously reported optical nucleation and annihilation. The material is then patterned into a wire, to combine the optical manipulation with current-induced skyrmion motion. These results establish a route toward opto-spintronic skyrmion devices in which light programs the internal state of a skyrmion and electrical currents control its position.
summary: This research demonstrates a novel opto-spintronic device concept where magnetic skyrmions can be programmed by light and controlled by electricity. Using a multilayer film, the authors achieved deterministic switching of the skyrmion's internal core polarity with a single ultrafast laser pulse. This allows for light to set the internal state while current controls the physical movement, paving the way for advanced memory applications.
main_problem: The goal is to develop a deterministic, multi-state control mechanism for magnetic skyrmions by combining all-optical switching of their internal spin structure (polarity) with established current-induced motion.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated that a single, ultrafast laser pulse can deterministically toggle the core polarity of magnetic skyrmions in a patterned multilayer structure, which can then be combined with electrical currents to control the skyrmion's position.
method: The study uses ultrafast laser pulses (30 fs) to induce All-Optical Helicity-Independent Switching (AO-HIS) in a patterned multilayer film, followed by applying DC currents to observe deterministic skyrmion motion.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Pt/Ir/CoB/Gd/Pt multilayer stack, engineered to stabilize magnetic skyrmions and enable AO-HIS. The structure is patterned into wires to facilitate the combination of optical programming and electrical transport.
key_observables: Skyrmion core polarity (toggled by light), skyrmion position (controlled by current), switching thresholds (Fth, FMD), and the stability of the magnetic textures.
important_parameters: Ultrafast laser pulse fluence (e.g., 3.98 mJ cm^-2 for switching), DC current density (e.g., 5.9 x 10^9 A m^-2), and temperature (up to 350 K).
main_assumptions: The ability to combine stabilization and AO-HIS depends sensitively on the material stack composition; furthermore, the measurements do not resolve the full reversal dynamics, only the before and after states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the concept sequence: (a) writing skyrmions via pulse-train scanning, (b) single-pulse reversal of core polarity, and (c) subsequent current-induced motion in a patterned wire. Other figures detail the AO-HIS operating window and thermal stability.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the material platform and the AO-HIS mechanism using single pulses. It then demonstrates the writing of skyrmions optically, followed by combining this optical programming step with established current-driven motion in a patterned wire device.
why_interesting: This work represents a significant step toward integrating multiple control mechanisms (optical, electrical) into a single spintronic device, which is highly relevant for developing next-generation memory or logic elements.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Concept and material platform. a-c) Schematic of the opto-electrical skyrmion manip- ulation sequence: pulse-train laser excitation writes skyrmions (a), a single femtosecond laser pulse reverses the skyrmion core polarity (b), and current-induced spin-orbit torques transport the skyrmion in a wire (c). d) Device concept illustrating that light pulses program the inter- nal core state while electrical current controls the skyrmion position. e) Multilayer structure Ta/Pt/Ir/CoB/Gd/Pt, where CoB and Gd thicknesses are tuned to combine interfacial DMI, perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and AO-HIS.

Figure 2: AO-HIS operating window in the CoB/Gd skyrmion platform. a–c) Kerr microscopy images of switched regions obtained at representative fluences, showing deterministic toggle switching below the multidomain threshold and multidomain formation above FMD = 7.96 ± 0.6 mJ cm−2. The images correspond to increasing fluence, as indicated by the arrows. d) Size of the single-pulse switched domains as a function of laser fluence for the continuous-film sample. The major and minor ellipse axes, Dx and Dy, are fitted using d = D[log(F/Fth)]1/2 [37], yielding an AO-HIS threshold of Fth = 3.98 mJ cm−2.

Figure 3: a)-c) Kerr microscopy snapshots of magnetic skyrmions nucleated by pulse-train laser scanning, showing the written skyrmionic textures. Snapshots are taken as the laser spot is swept from left to right, as illustrated by the positions of the dashed ellipses. d) Final state, after nucleation. Laser parameters: τ = 7.5 ps, F = 13.28 mJ cm−2, and f = 5 kHz. Scale bar: 50 µm.

Figure 4: Single-pulse optical reversal of skyrmion core polarity. a) Initial Kerr microscopy image of laser-written skyrmions in the continuous-film sample. b) Image acquired after one 30 fs laser pulse applied to the dashed elliptical region, showing reversal of the selected skyrmion core. c) Image acquired after a second pulse applied to a central region, showing simultaneous reversal of two skyrmion cores. The dashed ellipses indicate the approximate optical switching footprint corresponding to the AO-HIS threshold. A more accurate evaluation of the irradiated areas can be found in Figure S3.
